records.scope: Flask application implementing the nfl.com mirror: the utility bar, live scoreboard ribbon, shield header and mega nav chrome; week-by-week scores for all 18 weeks of the 2026 season; game centers with quarter scores, at-a-glance comparisons, team leaders and injury blocks; standings; 32 club pages with rosters and schedules; the scored player directory and player pages with career stats; the newsroom with pagination; the four-channel video hub; 11 stat leaderboards; the Week 3 injury report; the September transaction log; the NFL+ plans page with the full subscription checkout chain (card validation, order confirmation, subscription management); account personalization (favorite team, newsletter) and site-wide scored search.

Deterministic build-time and boot-time seeder. All content rows come from the tracked source_data/ snapshots; every seed function early-returns on a populated DB and every date is pinned relative to MIRROR_DATE (2026-09-24) so the SQLite seed is byte-reproducible on every build. Benchmark users use a frozen password digest.

Frozen snapshots of the live nfl.com and api.nfl.com as served on 2026-09-23/24: 32 team records (colors, conference/division, coach, stadium, owners, post-Week-2 records), 2,538 rostered players with headshot ids, 272 regular-season games with scores/quarters/attendance/weather for the completed weeks, 82 news articles with full bodies, 280 videos with thumbnails, 11 league-leader stat tables (25 rows each), the Week 3 injury report (259 rows), 86 September transactions, the four NFL+ plans with real prices, and per-player career/game-log tables for the 65 featured stat pages.
Per-file inventory (bytes, SHA-256, upstream source URL) for every managed image under static/images/; enforced by the image build's check_asset_inventory.py gate.
The 32 club logos served by static.www.nfl.com/league/api/clubs/logos (SVG or PNG per team, exactly as the CDN serves them).

Real player headshots served by static.www.nfl.com at the t_thumb_squared_2x roster transform (and the t_headshot_desktop transform for the 75 featured player pages), one per rostered player whose upstream image resolves.
Editorial art for the newsroom at the t_editorial_landscape_12_desktop transform, as rendered by the live article pages.
Video thumbnails served by static.www.nfl.com at the hub and channel transforms, one per seeded video.

The NFL shield, conference marks, broadcaster logos (CBS/FOX/NBC/ESPN/Prime Video/NFL+ Premium), NFL Network and RedZone marks, TNF/SNF/MNF marks, social icons, partner logos and the NFL+ marketing art, all fetched from the upstream global asset paths the live pages reference.
Hand-written stylesheet reproducing the captured nfl.com design language (navy #013369 / red #D50A0A palette, utility bar, scores ribbon, card grids, data tables, plan cards, footer).

Jinja templates reproducing the captured upstream layout: base chrome with ribbon/nav/footer/tracking banner, homepage with hero and My Team module, scoreboard and game centers, standings, club/roster/schedule pages, player directory and player pages, newsroom and articles, video hub and video pages, stat leaderboards, injuries, transactions, NFL+ plans and checkout, account surfaces, search results, and 404/500 handlers.

Pytest suite: tasks.jsonl contract (five basic keys only, no ground-truth leaks, sequential ids, declared-port URLs, ≤100-word prompts, multi-domain coverage), route/behavior robustness against a scratch DB (auth, subscribe chain with card validation, filters, scored search, personalization, newsletter), seed determinism (byte-reproducible build), and image-reference integrity (every served path exists, inventory covers every shipped file, no placeholders).

The capture and build pipeline (gitignored outputs): Playwright captures for the weekly-game-details API (weeks 1-18), team pages, player stat pages, transactions tabs, subscription data and missing recon; build_source_data.py turning the raw captures into the tracked source_data/ snapshots; harvest_images.py downloading every real upstream image and writing image_manifest.json / asset_inventory.json.

Resumable raw upstream captures (gitignored, never shipped): rendered page HTML/text for every mirrored surface, the weekly API JSONs, roster pages, 82 article pages, 75 player stat pages, injuries, transactions, subscription data, and reference screenshots.
